title: Statistical Landscape Exploration and Weak-Field Defects in Selective Oscillator Ising Machines
abstract: Oscillator Ising machines (OIMs) provide an analog dynamical approach to combinatorial optimization, but comparatively little is known about the statistical structure of the ensembles they generate. Using the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) spin-glass model, we introduce a selective oscillator scheme, OIM+, in which successive annealing epochs are combined with energy-based elimination and repopulation of replicas. We characterize the resulting states through overlap distributions, Hamming distances, hierarchical clustering, and local-field statistics. OIM+ explores structured low-energy regions while retaining a nontrivial ensemble of configurations despite repeated selection. We identify sparse weak-local-field residual defects as a characteristic limitation of the dynamics. A short Metropolis-Hastings refinement preferentially corrects these defects, indicating that the oscillator dynamics performs the dominant collective exploration while the remaining corrections are predominantly local. The weak fields arise mainly from cancellation among competing interaction terms rather than uniformly weak couplings. The same behavior persists for an antiferromagnetically biased SK ensemble, where the hybrid method reaches a pooled mean energy comparable to a substantially longer pure Metropolis anneal. The complete protocol also achieves competitive performance on standard G-set Max-Cut benchmarks. These results suggest a natural division of labor between collective analog search and targeted local refinement.
summary: This paper analyzes how selective oscillator dynamics explores the complex energy landscape of spin-glass models. It identifies that the dynamics excels at global, collective exploration, leaving behind only weak, local defects. By combining this analog search with a local refinement step, the protocol achieves competitive performance on hard optimization problems like Max-Cut.
main_problem: The study characterizes the statistical structure of ensembles generated by Oscillator Ising Machines (OIMs) when exploring complex, frustrated energy landscapes, moving beyond simple energy minimization.
main_result: The selective oscillator dynamics performs the dominant collective exploration, while residual errors manifest as sparse weak-local-field defects, which can be corrected by local Metropolis refinement.
method: The authors employ a selective multi-epoch annealing protocol (OIM+) on the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin-glass model, followed by a local Metropolis-Hastings refinement.
model_or_system: The system uses Oscillator Ising Machines (OIMs) coupled to the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) spin-glass model, which models frustrated optimization problems like Max-Cut.
key_observables: Overlap distributions, Hamming distances, hierarchical clustering, local-field statistics, and the final cut value on G-set benchmarks.
important_parameters: The annealing schedule involves multiple epochs with time-dependent noise and selection criteria; the comparison is made against pure Metropolis annealing.
main_assumptions: The analysis suggests a natural division of labor between the collective analog search (OIM+) and targeted local refinement (MH).
figures_summary: Figures detail the selective multi-epoch annealing schedule for OIM+, showing the progression of annealing parameters over time.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the OIM+ protocol for exploring the SK model's statistical structure, identifies the weak-field defect mechanism, and then validates the complete hybrid protocol (OIM+ + MH) on standard G-set Max-Cut benchmarks.
why_interesting: The concept of using analog dynamics (oscillators) for collective exploration, followed by targeted digital refinement, provides a blueprint for hybrid quantum/classical optimization algorithms relevant to quantum computation.
